raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Single-node device-side feature transport — provide an NPU-capable alternative to CUDA IPC for transferring multimodal feature tensors between local processes*).

## Motivation

`--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` currently requires NVIDIA CUDA: the feature pool, proxy lifecycle, and device primitives are hardcoded against `torch.cuda.*` and CUDA IPC handles. On Ascend NPU, multimodal features produced by the tokenizer process must therefore detour through host memory (CPU transport) even when both processes sit on the same node and the features already live in device HBM.

This PR makes the existing `cuda_ipc` transport NPU-capable with **zero behavior change on CUDA**. CUDA keeps the bounded pool + lease/ACK design unchanged; NPU follows the official torch_npu IPC recipe (`docs/memory_sharing_ipc.md`, method two): `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor` → `rebuild_npu_tensor`, using public APIs only (no undocumented ACL calls).

## Design

- **No new CLI option**: NPU reuses the existing `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` entry, gated per platform.
- **Features never leave NPU HBM**: the producer packs `(rebuild_func, args)` via the public `reduce_tensor` and pickles it into `proxy_state["ipc_extra"]["npu_ipc_payload"]` — a ~377 B descriptor regardless of feature size. The consumer rebuilds the tensor on its own device by redirecting the storage device index (`args[6]`), guarded by a layout/type check so an upstream layout change degrades with a warning instead of silently corrupting an unrelated argument.
- **No pool on NPU**: zero HBM reservation, no lease/ACK bookkeeping; the KV-cache budget is no longer deducted for a pool that does not exist.
- **Platform branches stay in one place**: the new `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc_bridge.py` hosts `IS_NPU` detection, the torch_npu `reductions` patch import (single side-effect point), device primitives (`make_device` / `current_device` / `device_guard` / `is_device_tensor`), and the pack/rebuild pair. All other touched files stay host-agnostic.

## Roadmap item coverage

| Roadmap requirement | How it is covered |
|---|---|
| Bounded memory use | No pool on NPU → zero HBM reservation; `kv_cache_configurator` skips the pool deduction on NPU, recovering ~2–3 GB of usable KV |
| Tensor lifetime | torch_npu ref-counter keeps the shared block alive while consumers exist; rebuilt tensors verified bitwise-identical even after the producer drops its source tensor |
| Cancellation | `cancel_proxy` handles NPU proxies on the processor rollback path |
| Pool exhaustion | Not applicable — NPU has no pool; the failure mode is `reduce_tensor` raising, which falls back to the CPU transport |
| Fallback to CPU path | `wrap_tensor` returns `None` on any pack failure → CPU transport; A/B runs show 0 fallbacks |
| Transfer cost & TTFT comparison | Benchmarks below |

## Modifications

- **NEW** `srt/multimodal/transport/npu_ipc_bridge.py` (112 lines): platform detection + patch import, device primitives, `npu_ipc_pack_tensor` / `npu_ipc_rebuild_tensor` with `args[6]` redirect + layout guard
- `srt/multimodal/transport/cuda_ipc.py`: NPU branches on the shared transport — producer pack + proxy shell, `cancel_proxy`, `_restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state`, consumer rebuild in `reconstruct_on_target_device` (cached, returns before the CUDA-pool fields), borrow/lease paths report unsupported so the scheduler falls back to reconstruct
- `srt/utils/msgpack_utils.py`: call `_restore_npu_ipc_proxy_state` after msgpack decode
- `srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`: gate device-IPC wrapping on `is_device_tensor`; skip CUDA-pool reservation logs on NPU
- `srt/models/qwen3_vl.py`: resolve the visual-tower device via the bridge; treat `cuda`/`npu` alike in the on-device check
- `srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`: skip the pool KV deduction on NPU
- `srt/arg_groups/serving_hook.py`: platform check relaxation + per-platform pool-reservation logs

On CUDA, every modified call site either executes identical code or is unreachable — behavior is unchanged.

## Benchmarks (Ascend 910, CANN 9.1.0, torch_npu 2.10.0, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking)

Transfer-level, two processes, 16 producer threads, in-flight depth 8, 800 frames per group:

| Feature size | CPU ms/frame | NPU IPC ms/frame | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5 MiB | 0.98 | 0.52 | 46.8% |
| 18.4 MiB | 13.07 | 0.54 | 95.9% |
| 47.6 MiB | 56.30 | 0.52 | 99.1% |

IPC cost is constant (~0.52 ms/frame — only the 377 B descriptor crosses processes) while CPU transfer is strictly linear in feature size.

End-to-end (4×1024² images per request, 16 concurrency, 90 s): 0 errors and 0 fallbacks on both arms; p50 delta −13.5% is within the noise band (p99 +11.1%, single round, transfer explains ~0.4% of end-to-end latency at this scale) and is not claimed as a win.

Accuracy: MMBench EN DEV v1.1, 1292 questions, CircularEval, greedy decoding, `cuda_ipc` vs `cpu` on the same node with a position-swap control over 3 rounds — no transport-induced accuracy delta (observed ±0.7 pp shifts do not follow the transport arm and flip sign after swapping dies).

## Test plan

- [x] `py_compile` on all touched files
- [x] Functional smoke on Ascend: real image request end-to-end, `NPU IPC rebuild success` in scheduler log, 0 CPU fallbacks / 0 tracebacks
- [x] Cross-process bitwise consistency of rebuilt tensors
- [x] 16-concurrency A/B (`cuda_ipc` vs `cpu`): 0 errors, 0 fallbacks on both arms
- [x] MMBench accuracy A/B as above

+"""Cross-platform helpers for the multimodal feature transport.
+
+CUDA and Ascend NPU pool implementations agree on a small set of primitives:
+device introspection, stream/device guards, and the reduce/rebuild pair.
+Ascend NPU does *not* use the pool: it follows the official torch_npu IPC docs
+(``docs/memory_sharing_ipc.md``, method two) and transports a tensor through the
+public ``torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor`` -> ``rebuild_npu_tensor``
+pair, so no undocumented ACL API is needed.  The CUDA value-signal primitives
+used by the bounded pool stay in ``transport/memory_pool.py``, and the
+CUDA-only storage share/open helpers stay in ``transport/cuda_ipc.py``.
+
+Every platform branch is kept in one place so callers stay host agnostic.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Iterator
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _npu_available() -> bool:
+    npu_mod = getattr(torch, "npu", None)
+    if npu_mod is None:
+        return False
+    return bool(getattr(npu_mod, "is_available", lambda: False)())
+
+
+IS_NPU = _npu_available()
+
+if IS_NPU:
+    # Importing this module installs the ``reduce_tensor`` / ``reduce_storage``
+    # patches onto ``torch.multiprocessing.reductions`` through torch_npu's
+    # normal import path and triggers lazy device init.
+    import torch_npu.multiprocessing.reductions  # noqa: F401
+
+# Position of the storage device index inside the ``reduce_tensor`` argument
+# tuple produced by torch_npu's multiprocessing reductions patch.
+_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX = 6
+
+
+def is_device_tensor(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``tensor`` lives on the accelerator of this node."""
+    return tensor.device.type == device_type()
+
+
+def device_type() -> str:
+    return "npu" if IS_NPU else "cuda"
+
+
+def device_str(device_id: int) -> str:
+    return f"{device_type()}:{device_id}"
+
+
+def make_device(device_id: int) -> torch.device:
+    return torch.device(device_str(device_id))
+
+
+def current_device() -> int:
+    if IS_NPU:
+        return torch.npu.current_device()
+    return torch.cuda.current_device()
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def device_guard(device_id: int) -> Iterator[None]:
+    if IS_NPU:
+        ctx = torch.npu.device(device_id)
+    else:
+        ctx = torch.cuda.device(device_id)
+    with ctx:
+        yield
+
+
+def npu_ipc_pack_tensor(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> tuple:
+    """Prepare a tensor for cross-process transport on this node.
+
+    Returns ``(reconstruct_func, args)``.  On Ascend NPU this is the public
+    ``reduce_tensor`` exported by ``torch.multiprocessing.reductions`` (patched
+    by torch_npu), whose ``args[6]`` holds the storage device index.  On CUDA
+    the tuple is returned as a fallback but the pool path is preferred there.
+    """
+    from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor
+
+    return reduce_tensor(tensor)
+
+
+def npu_ipc_rebuild_tensor(func, args: tuple, rebuild_device_idx: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reconstruct a tensor previously prepared by :func:`npu_ipc_pack_tensor`.
+
+    ``args[6]`` is the storage device index; it is redirected to
+    ``rebuild_device_idx`` so the shared storage is opened on the consumer's
+    device (single-node IPC).  The position is verified before being rewritten
+    so that a layout change in ``reduce_tensor`` cannot silently corrupt an
+    unrelated argument.
+    """
+    redirected = list(args)
+    if len(redirected) > _NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX and isinstance(
+        redirected[_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX], int
+    ):
+        redirected[_NPU_IPC_DEVICE_ARG_INDEX] = rebuild_device_idx
+    else:
+        logger.warning(
+            "NPU IPC payload args layout changed (len=%d); "
+            "rebuilding on the producer device instead of %d.",
+            len(redirected),
+            rebuild_device_idx,
+        )
+    with device_guard(rebuild_device_idx):
+        return func(*redirected)

+        # and owns no pool lease, so the consumer-side state has to be rebuilt
+        # from the serialized proxy instead of the fields set above.
